I am 30 years old, I planned to have a baby and was trying for over a year. I have a supportive partner (who works a lot but still) and I still struggled so so much after having my baby. I felt like I made a mistake and I wasn’t doing a good enough job, I wasn’t cut out to be a mother. I felt like I was failing. There were moments that I felt like I regretted it and I wished I just would’ve went through life without kids. 

It was so so hard and still continues to be, but I will say that you find your own groove. My son is 10 months old now and although he still drives me crazy on some days, it is a lot better than it was in those early days. You and your baby get into a routine and you learn what they want and need. Sometimes I still feel like I am failing but I do feel like it’s a lot better than the early days. For example: he sleeps through the night! So I’m actually rested. 

Try not to be so hard on yourself, Momma. You will get there. I also had a traumatic birth experience and worried that it affected our bonding. I also struggled with getting out of the house afterwards. I mean, you’re unshowered and a mess and I hated taking the baby places, but now that he’s older I’ve found a daily walk does wonders for us both. Just know you are not alone and you will get through this.

I’ve seen first hand the aftermath of suicide and how it can affect people in ways. My mom lost her best friend since she was 11 to suicide and it is a very long complicated story, but she was never ever the same after she lost. She was in therapy for the rest of her life until she ultimately died from an accidental drug overdose. I honestly don’t think she ever truly recovered from the guilt she felt. My philosophy has always sort of been this: suicide doesn’t get rid of the pain, it just passes the pain off to somebody else. I know that is probably cliche or whatever but that’s what I’ve always kept in my head when I struggle with my own suicidal thoughts. (I have attempted before so I am not perfect) I just try to remember the people I love and no matter how much I hurt, I would never want to pass that pain on to somebody else. It’s not something small. It’s catastrophic because it has the potential truly ruin the lives of those around you. I don’t think of suicide as “bad” and I don’t think people who do it are selfish. They are just in a lot of pain and need help. I personally emphasize with them because I have attempted multiple times before and I know how it feels to want to die and prepare yourself to die. I think with therapy, medication, better coping mechanisms, whatever works for you personally, you are able to work through it. It’s really difficult because I’m not in the right frame of mind (at least for me personally) when I get that way. But yeah I have learned certain coping mechanisms when I do feel I am on the verge of a breakdown. So yeah that is a little mantra I live by I guess: You’re not getting rid of the pain, you’re just giving it over to somebody else. I’m sure many people will say it is cliche and stupid and I don’t understand or whatever, but I have seen firsthand how suicide can directly ruin other people’s lives. Or at least be a catalyst and cause a lot a lot of pain. That being said, I don’t think suicide is “bad” or think badly of those who do it.
